summary: Iteration 29 — Full E2E backend functional audit (round 1 of 2) of Orrbbit across all 9 areas requested. 54/56 tests PASS, 2 skipped (intentional: high-risk admin action lacked a live QA_ target; password_resets collection is not exposed via the DB viewer whitelist — good). Overall backend health: EXCELLENT (96%+). Live email sends kept at 1 (forgot-password to delivered@resend.dev). Only material defect found: registration has NO server-side minimum password length — accepts '1'.

minor.issue: MEDIUM — RegisterIn Pydantic model does not enforce a minimum password length. Server accepts passwords as short as '1' and hashes them via bcrypt. Login then works fine. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:509-550 (register endpoint), and the RegisterIn model near the top of the file. Reset flow correctly enforces min 8 (password_reset.py:48). Recommend adding min_length=8 to RegisterIn.password.

LOW — Field-name inconsistency: this endpoint expects {photo: url} while every other place uses {photo_url: url}. Documented actual behaviour: 422 'Field required' when photo_url is sent. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:631-641 (PhotoIn model).

LOW/INFO — Message body containing spammy/scam terms ('buy viagra crypto scam bitcoin') was accepted (200). _check_banned may not include these. If banned-word filter is intended to catch such payloads, expand the list. Reference: server.py:_check_banned (~line 2011).

LOW — Uses update_one with filter {id, to_user_id: caller}; silently no-ops (returns ok:true) if caller isn't the recipient rather than 404. Not a security hole (can't modify others' pings) but inconsistent with dismiss/decline which return 404. Reference: server.py:1091-1094.

INFO — Response contains 'distance' (rounded to whole meters) and 'bearing' but never raw lat/lng of other users. Distance is exact-to-meter (not further fuzzed). Code does NOT claim fuzzing, so behaviour matches design. No leak.

INFO — Admin database viewer correctly redacts sensitive values: hashed_password value is replaced with '•••redacted•••'. No bcrypt hashes, no plaintext passwords, no reset codes leak. Field key still visible; harmless.
INFO — Not exposed via the DB viewer collection whitelist (returns 400). This is a positive security choice — password reset codes/hashes are not browsable through the control centre.

security_findings.result: PASS — regular user JWT returns 401/403 on /api/control/users.
PASS — identical response for existing and nonexistent emails.

security_findings.check: Auth endpoints leak no stack traces
security_findings.result: PASS — checked /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register error paths for 'traceback', 'file "', 'line N', 'at 0x'. All clean.

PASS — no bcrypt hash ($2b$ / $2a$) appears in /api/control/db/users response.
PASS — no lat/lng of other users; only distance (meters) and bearing (deg).

security_findings.check: email_events ctx has no API key

security_findings.result: PASS — DELETE /api/users/me on a demo returns 403.

action_items: MEDIUM: Add password strength minimum (min_length=8) to RegisterIn.password in /app/backend/server.py (line ~509 area). Currently only reset-password enforces this — meaning any client hitting the API directly can create accounts with 1-char passwords.

LOW: Normalise the photo add endpoint to accept 'photo_url' (or update the docs/frontend) — /app/backend/server.py:631 (PhotoIn currently expects {photo: str}) is inconsistent with every other user-facing schema.

LOW: Consider extending _check_banned wordlist to catch obvious spam/scam terms (viagra, bitcoin, crypto, scam) if that's the intent of the filter — currently only user-supplied test payload with these words was accepted.
LOW: Make POST /api/pings/{id}/dismiss return 404 when the ping is not the caller's (parity with /decline). Not a security hole, just inconsistent.
INFO: The 'user_id' passed to POST /api/connect/request when it's a completely non-existent UUID correctly returns 404. Same for /api/professional/connect. Both good.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:187 public_user() — correctly strips hashed_password before returning. Verified on register/login/demo-login/me responses.
server.py:897, 1215, 1232 — every db.users.find*() call that returns users to callers explicitly projects out {hashed_password: 0}. Consistent pattern.
professional_flow.py:57 _user_brief() — also projects out hashed_password. Good.
server.py:579-597 delete_account() — comprehensive cleanup: user + pings + matches + meetups + saved + blocks + hides; reports intentionally retained anonymously. Correct.
password_reset.py:29-30 _hash_code() — SHA-256 hash of the 6-digit code; only code_hash stored in db.password_resets. Correct.
server.py:_validate_connect_target — correctly rejects self, hidden/banned, paused/ghost, blocked. Same helper used by both /connect/request and legacy /matches.
professional_flow.py:64 _assert_participant() — enforces requester_id or professional_id membership on every session-scoped endpoint. Non-participant access verified to return 403.

rca_of_issue: Registration password minimum: RegisterIn (Pydantic model in server.py) does not include min_length on the password field, so Pydantic accepts any string >= 0 chars. bcrypt happily hashes '1'. LoginIn is symmetric (no min), so short passwords also succeed on login. Fix: add Field(min_length=8, max_length=128) to RegisterIn.password (mirror the ResetIn constraint in password_reset.py:48). No data migration needed.
